name: Polar sea ice
summary: Arctic sea ice 1.91M km² and Antarctic 1.11M km² below average on 21 Nov; neither at a record low
state: On 21 Nov Arctic sea-ice extent was 9.09 million km², about 1.91 million km² below the 1981–2010 average and the third lowest for the date (NSIDC). Antarctic extent was 14.21 million km², about 1.11 million km² below average and the fifth lowest for the date. Both are past the −1.0 million km² Watch line, and neither pole is at a record low.
for_you: Low sea ice is a long-term climate indicator rather than an immediate hazard; it affects polar shipping, wildlife and regional weather.
rubric_hit: Arctic anomaly −1.91M km² below −1.0M Watch line; no record low
why: Sea ice reflects sunlight and regulates ocean circulation; record lows accelerate warming.
drivers: Air and ocean temperatures, winds, season.

rubric.alert: Either pole at a record low for the calendar date.
rubric.normal: Arctic and Antarctic extent anomalies both above −1.0 million km² vs 1981–2010.
